translations.text: Chronicle: From the creation of the world to the year 1087 of Alexander. First Part.
[?] We begin with the course of the creation of the world [?] we set down in this book, so that the reader's mind and the listener's hearing will not be confused.
In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. The earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the surface of the deep.
And the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters. God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light. God saw that the light was good.
God separated the light from the darkness. God called the light day, and the darkness he called night. There was evening and there was morning: one day.
These things were created on the first day, that is, on Sunday. On the second day God said, “Let there be a dome in the midst of the waters,
and let it separate water from water.” God made the dome and separated the waters below the dome
from the waters above the dome. And it was so. He called the dome heaven. There was evening and there was morning: the second day.
These things he created on the second day. On the third day God said, “Let the waters below heaven be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear.”
And it was so. God called the dry land earth, and the gathering of the waters he called seas. God saw that it was good. And God said,
“Let the earth bring forth vegetation: plants yielding seed according to their kinds, and fruit trees bearing fruit according to their kinds, with their seed in them, upon the earth.” And it was so.
The earth brought forth vegetation: plants yielding seed according to their kinds, and trees bearing fruit according to their kinds, with their seed in them, upon the earth. God saw that it was good.
There was evening and there was morning: the third day. On the fourth day God said, “Let there be lights in the dome of heaven to separate day from night.
Let them serve as signs and mark seasons, days, and years. Let them shine in the dome of heaven to give light upon the earth.” And it was so.
God also created two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night, and the stars.
God placed them in the dome of heaven to give light upon the earth, to rule over day and night, and to separate light from darkness.
God saw that it was good. There was evening and there was morning: the fourth day. Again, on the fifth day God said,
“Let the waters swarm with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the face of the dome of heaven.”
God created the great sea monsters and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarmed, according to their kinds,
and every winged bird according to its kind. God saw that it was good. God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful
and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let the birds multiply on the earth.” There was evening and there was morning: the fifth day.
On the sixth day, which is Friday—on it Adam was created, on it the crucifixion took place at Golgotha, and on it the world was redeemed—
God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, crawling creatures, and wild animals of the earth according to their kinds.” And it was so.
God made the living creatures according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and all the crawling creatures of the earth according to their kinds. God saw that it was good.
Concerning the formation of humanity, God said, “Let us make human beings in our image, according to our likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of heaven.

And over the livestock, all the animals of the earth, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth. Understand, discerning reader, that creation was created first, and only afterward, at the end, Adam himself.
This was so that he would not dare to say, “I too created everything, just as he did.” It is written: “By the word of the Lord the heavens were made,
and by the breath of his mouth all their hosts.” And again: “He spoke, and they came into being; he commanded, and they were created. He established them forever and ever.”
Here, however, it was not like that. He did (not) say, “Let them come into being,” but, “Come, let us make a human being in our image, according to our likeness.” There it was a word;
here it was the handiwork of the Godhead, not a command. Concerning the angels and all the heavenly orders, he said that they were created by the breath of his mouth.
Here the whole Trinity moves in majesty to form the human being. Heretics and pagans ought to be ashamed at this statement—
those who oppose the Son and the Spirit and say that the Son and the Spirit do not share the Father's essence, when they hear
the Father calling out to the Son and the Spirit and saying, “Come.” He did not say “Come” in the singular, as to one, but “Come” in the plural, as to two.
And he who gave the command, as the head of the three, said, “Come, let us make a human being in our image, according to our likeness.”
And again, making known that the Trinity is one nature, and not three gods or three essences, he said:
“And God created Adam in his image; in the image of God he created him. Male and female he created them. God blessed them, and God said to them:
‘Be fruitful and multiply. Fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the heavens, the livestock, the wild animals,
and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.’ And God said, ‘Look, I have given you every plant that is sown over the face of the whole earth.’”
Notice again that, in addressing the human being, it does not say, “They said,” as in the earlier statement, “Come, let us make,” but, “God said,”
showing that the Trinity is one nature. And again he said: “The Lord God formed Adam, dust from the ground,
and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and Adam became a living soul.” Adam was created on this very sixth day, and on it he transgressed the commandment.
On it our Lord was hung on the tree, and on it salvation came to the whole world. On the Sabbath God rested from all the works he had done.
God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it he rested from all the works he had created. [?] Our Lord also rested in the tomb,
and laid aside all the sufferings he had borne on Golgotha. On it the whole company of captives whom he brought back from the captor's hands also found rest.
In the year 230 from the creation of the world and of Adam, Seth was born. And in the year 435,
Seth fathered Enosh. In the year 625, Enosh fathered Kenan. And in the year 795,
Mahalalel was born to Kenan. In the year 930, Adam departed from this world.
His sons embalmed him and placed him [in the Cave of Treasures] on the mountain called Shir, which is [on the] eastern [side], facing the great ocean.
In this very Cave of Treasures, Adam and his son Seth placed gold, myrrh, and frankincense in bags. He also sealed them with his signet ring and with the signet ring of his son Seth.
He wrote documents and also instructed his sons that whichever of them lived at the time when a spear of fire, with a star of light at its tip, appeared over the entrance to the Cave of Treasures,
Let us take these offerings and follow the star wherever it goes, and offer them to the king who is born there.
Now it was in this very cave, where Adam placed gold, myrrh, and frankincense in honor of Christ and because of his birth in the flesh, that he was laid.

I have written these few things about why that cave was called the Cave of Treasures, so that you may know and understand that it was because of this gold, myrrh, and frankincense, which were brought to our Lord at his birth,
which had been deposited there by Adam and Seth, that it was called the Cave of Treasures. In the year 960, Mahalalel fathered Jared.
In Jared’s fortieth year, the first millennium was completed, according to the reckoning of the Seventy. In the year 1,082, Enoch was born.
In the year 1,142, Seth departed from this world. In the year 1,247, Methuselah was born to Enoch.
In the year 1,340, Enosh departed from this world. His sons embalmed him and laid him in the Cave of Treasures. In the year one thousand four hundred
and fourteen, Lamech was born to Methuselah. In the year one thousand five hundred [?], Noah was born to Lamech.
In the year 1,690, Mahalalel departed from this world. His sons embalmed him and laid him in the Cave of Treasures beside his ancestors.
In the year 1,535, Kenan departed from this world and was laid in the Cave of Treasures. In the year 1,602, Noah was born.
In the year 1,902, Jared departed from this world on the thirteenth of the month of Adar, on Friday at sunset,
weeping in distress and great sorrow over the descent of the sons of Seth to the daughters of Cain. [?], Methuselah, Lamech, and Noah embalmed him.
Mourning was also held for him for forty days, and they buried him in the Cave of Treasures. In the year 1,407, Enoch was taken away.
In the year 2,216, Methuselah departed from this world on the twenty-first of Elul, on Thursday,
twenty-six years before the Flood [?], and was laid in the Cave of Treasures. In the three hundred and fifty-eighth year of Noah’s life,
the second millennium was completed, according to the translation of the Seventy. In Lamech’s one hundred and twenty-sixth year, the first millennium was completed,
according to the Hebrew reckoning of the Jews. In Noah’s two hundred and ninety-third year, the first millennium was completed according to the Hebrew reckoning of the Samaritans.
When Noah was [?] years old, he took as his wife Heikal, the daughter of Namus, the son of Enoch, Methuselah’s brother.
God revealed to him the flood that he was preparing to bring. He spoke with him [?] and said to him, “In one hundred and thirty years from now, I will bring a flood. But make
yourself an ark to save the members of your household. Build it down below, in the midst of the camp of Cain’s descendants. Its timbers are to be cut from this mountain.
This is how it shall be: its length shall be three hundred cubits, measured by your cubit; its width, fifty; and its height, thirty. Finish it to one cubit at the top.
Make three decks in it: the lower one for wild animals and livestock, the middle one for birds, and the upper one for the members of your household.
Make storage places in it for water and chambers for provisions. Make yourself a sounding board from boxwood, wood that does not rot.
Its length shall be three cubits and its width a cubit and a half, with a mallet made from the same wood. Strike it three times a day:
once in the morning, so that the craftsmen may gather to work on the ark; at midday, for their meal; and once in the evening, so that they may rest.”
And when they hear the sound of your hammering and say to you, ‘What is this you are doing?’ tell them, ‘God is bringing a flood of water.’
And he did everything God commanded him. Three sons were born to him over the course of a hundred years.
And he took wives for them from the daughters of Methuselah. And in the year two thousand two hundred and thirty-eight,
in the month of Adar, on Sunday, the seventeenth day of the month, Lamech departed from this world, four years before the flood.
And he was laid in the Cave of Treasures. And in the year two thousand two hundred and four and two [?], the flood took place.
When the time for the flood to come upon the earth drew near, Noah entered the Cave of Treasures and kissed the holy bodies of Seth, Enosh, Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, Methuselah, and his father Lamech.
Noah carried Adam’s body, Shem the gold, Ham the myrrh, and Japheth the frankincense, and he went out of the Cave of Treasures.
They were weeping in grief and great sorrow, clothed in mourning, because they were being deprived of the dwelling place
so dear to their fathers. They all raised their eyes toward Paradise and wept in grief.
They wailed and said, ‘Farewell, holy Paradise, the first dwelling place of Adam our father! He left you alive, stripped and naked.
And behold, today he is being cut off from your surroundings, and in death he is being cast into exile abroad, he and his children,
into that land of curses, where his children will suffer pain, sickness, toil, weariness, and hardship.
Farewell, Cave of Treasures and holy bodies! Farewell, dwelling place and inheritance of our fathers!
Farewell, our fathers and our patriarchs! Pray for us, you who sleep in the dust, God’s friends and beloved ones.
Pray for the survivors who remain from all your descendants. Intercede for us in your prayers, you who please our Lord.
Farewell, righteous Enoch, servant of God! Intercede for us with your Lord. Farewell, holy mountain,
place of gathering [?] and haven of angels! You, our fathers, cry out in grief for us, for today you are being deprived of our company.
And we will wail in sorrow, for we are being cast into a desolate land, where their dwelling will be with wild animals. Woe to us, for we will no longer see the face of your inheritance!’
As they descended from the holy mountain, they kissed its stones and embraced its trees.
They went down into the plain in grief, weeping. Noah entered and placed the body of our father Adam [in the middle of the ark].
And he placed [these] offerings above him. On the tenth [day of the month of Iyar,] Noah [entered] the ark, on Wednesday.
On Friday he brought down the animals and birds. On the seventeenth day of the month, the floodgates of heaven were opened, and the depths
of the earth burst open. The great ocean surrounding the whole earth overflowed, and the storehouses of the winds and the gates of the storms were opened.
The ocean roared and overflowed. The descendants of Seth ran to the ark and pleaded with Noah to open it for them. As for climbing the mountains of Paradise,
they could not. The ark was closed and sealed, and the angel of the Lord stood on top of it, acting as its pilot.
When the Flood grew stronger against them, they began to drown in violent and terrifying torrents, and they were in severe distress.
And what blessed David said was fulfilled in them: “I said that you are gods, and you were called sons of the Most High.
But now that you have done this and loved the sexual immorality of Cain’s household, you will become like them and die as they died.
And I regard you as like Satan, one of the great ones who fell.” And the ark was lifted from the earth by the force of the waters.
All human beings were drowned in the waters, along with the animals, the birds, and everything that was on the face of the earth.
The waters rose above all the mountaintops, fifteen cubits by the measure of the Spirit, as it is written. And the waters lifted up the ark,
as the Flood carried it to the lower slopes of Paradise. When the ark had been blessed by Paradise, the Flood turned back to destroy the whole earth.
The ark flew on the wings of the wind above the Flood, from east to west and from north to south.

It traced a cross over the whole earth, above the Flood. Then the ark came to rest in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of that month, on the mountains of Qardu, and the mountaintops appeared.
After forty days, Noah opened the window of the ark that he had made. He sent out the raven, and it went out and did not return until the waters had dried up from the earth.
He sent out the dove from his presence to see whether the waters had receded from the face of the earth. But the dove found no resting place for the sole of its foot,
and it returned to him in the ark, because the waters were still over the face of the whole earth. He stretched out his hand and took it,
and brought it into the ark with him. He waited another seven days and again sent the dove out from the ark.
It came to him at evening time [?], and there was an olive leaf held in its beak. Noah knew that the waters had receded from the face of the earth.
He waited another seven days and again sent out the dove, and the dove did not return to him again.
In the year 2,203, Noah came out of the ark. The number of days that Noah was in the ark was
three hundred and eighty-two, because he entered on the tenth day of the second month, and on its seventeenth day the Flood came.
On the twenty-seventh day of that second month, which is Iyar, he came out. And in the year 2,204,
Arphaxad was born to Shem. From Adam to the Flood there were two thousand two hundred and forty-two years.
The Flood came in Noah’s six hundredth year and Shem’s hundredth year. And in the year 2,337,
Shelah was born. In the year 2,467, Eber was born to Shelah.
In the year 2,601, Eber fathered Peleg. At this time, human beings, in their madness, attempted to ascend to heaven.
The whole earth had one language and one form of speech. As they journeyed from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar,
and settled there. They said to one another, “Come, let us make bricks and burn them in the fire.” And they used
brick for stone, and lime for mortar. And they said, “Come, let us build ourselves a city and a tower with its top in heaven.”

“And let us make a name for ourselves, so that we will not be scattered over the face of the whole earth.” And the Lord came down to see the city and the tower that human beings were building. And the Lord said:
“Look, they are one people, and they all have one language. This is what they have planned to do. From now on, nothing they plan to do will be beyond their reach.
Come, let us go down and divide the languages there, so that no one will understand the language of his neighbor.”

Look here, you who contend against the Son and the Spirit: whom did he call, and who came down? And [?] the Spirit who divides languages in Babylon and in the upper room, for it is one and the same Spirit. And again he said:

“Look, Adam has become like one of us.” “Every matter shall be established,” it says, “by the testimony of two or three witnesses.” “Come, let us make humanity in our image, according to our likeness.”
“Look, Adam has become like one of us.” “Come, let us go down and divide the languages there.” These three testimonies bear witness to the Father, the Son, and the Spirit.
At this time the languages were confused, in the days of Peleg son of Eber. And in his time people were scattered over the face of the whole earth.
And they stopped building the city. For this reason it was called Babel, because there the Lord confused the languages of the whole earth.
At this time, too, the righteous Job is known to have lived, according to what the account says. He was the son of Joktan son of Eber, the brother of Peleg. Jacob also bears witness to this.
Nor was Moses, who wrote about him, unaware of his meaning when he listed the descendants of Edom down to Jobab son of Zerah, saying that this was Job.
That Jobab is also known to have lived in the days of Moses, as the book of Genesis bears witness. And in the year two [?] on Monday,
thousand five hundred and ninety-two, Noah departed from this world at the age of nine hundred and fifty years.
And in the year two thousand seven hundred and thirty-one, Reu was born to Peleg.
And in the year two thousand seven hundred and forty-four, Shem son of Noah departed from this world.
And in the year two thousand eight hundred and sixty-three, there was born [?]. And in the year two thousand eight hundred and sixty-three,
Serug was born to Reu. And in the ninety-fifth year of Serug’s life, the third millennium was completed.
At this time idols entered the world. From this point Noah’s descendants began to worship [?] idols entered the world.
From this point Noah’s descendants began to worship carved images, to do evil, to build cities, to take one another captive, and to wage war.
And in the thirty-first year of Serug’s life, the second millennium was completed according to the Hebrew reckoning of the Samaritans. In the year two thousand eight hundred and ninety-eight,
Nahor was born. In the year two thousand nine hundred and seventy-seven, Terah was born. And at the age of seventy, Terah fathered Abraham.
At this time Ninus was reigning over Nineveh. He built Nineveh and called it Nineveh after his own name.
And in the forty-third year of his reign, Abraham was born. This Ninus son of Belus was the first to reign over all Asia except India,
for fifty-two years. His forty-third year was Abraham’s first year.
And because we have not found a reckoning in which one account agrees with another, we set down here these earliest patriarchs as they appear in the book.
At the age of one hundred and thirty years, Adam fathered Seth. At the age of one hundred and thirty-five years, Seth fathered Enosh. Enosh was one hundred and ninety years old.
He fathered Kenan. Kenan was 170 years old when he fathered Mahalalel. Mahalalel was 165 years old when he fathered Jared.
In Jared’s fortieth year, the first thousand years were completed. Jared was 122 years old when he fathered Enoch.
He was 165 years old when he fathered Methuselah. Methuselah was 167 years old when he fathered Lamech.
Lamech was 188 years old when he fathered Noah. Noah was 500 years old when he fathered Shem.
In Noah’s 358th year, the second thousand years were completed. Shem was 102 years old when he fathered Arpachshad.
Arpachshad was 130 and [?] years old when he fathered Shelah. Shelah was 130 years old when he fathered Eber.
Eber was 134 years old when he fathered Peleg. Peleg was 130 years old when he fathered Reu.
Reu was [?] 132 years old when he fathered Serug. In Serug’s ninety-fifth year, the third thousand years were completed.
Serug was [one hundred and] thirty-five years old when he fathered Nahor. Nahor was seventy-nine years old when he fathered Terah.
Terah was seventy years old when he fathered Abram. Abram was one hundred [years] old when he fathered Isaac. Isaac was sixty years old when he fathered Jacob.
Jacob was eighty-six years old when he fathered Levi. Levi was forty-six years old when he fathered Levi.
Levi was forty-six years old when he fathered Kohath. Kohath was sixty years old when he fathered Amram. Amram was seventy years old when he fathered Moses.
In Moses’ eightieth year, the Israelites went out of Egypt. From here, the leaders. First, Moses: forty years.
Joshua: twenty-seven years. The Mesopotamians and Othniel, Joshua: forty years. The Moabites and Ehud: eighty years.
The Canaanites and Deborah and Barak: forty years. The Midianites and Gideon: forty years. Abimelech: three years. Tola: twenty
and three years. Jair: twenty-two [years]. In Jair’s nineteenth year, the fourth thousand years were completed.
The Ammonites and Jephthah: six years. Heshbon: seven years. [?]: eight years. The Philistines and Samson: twenty years.
Eli: forty years. Samuel and Saul: forty years. From here, the kings from the tribe of Judah.
David: forty years. Solomon: forty years. Rehoboam: seventeen years. Abijah: three years. Jehoshaphat: twenty-two years.
Jehoram: eight years. Ahaziah: one. Athaliah: seven years. Joash: forty years. Amaziah: twenty-nine years. Azariah: fifty-two
years. Jotham: sixteen years. Ahaz: sixteen years. Hezekiah: twenty-nine years. Manasseh: fifty-five years. Amon: [two] years.
Josiah: thirty-one years. Jehoahaz: three months. Jehoiakim: eleven years. Jeconiah: three months. Zedekiah: eleven years.
From here, the Persian kings. From Solomon’s fourth year until this point: 512 years.
Cyrus: thirty-four years. Ahasuerus Artaxerxes: forty-one years. Ahasuerus Darius: sixteen years. Artaxerxes: forty years.
Years. Arses: four years. Darius: six years. From here, the Macedonian kings. Alexander: six [years].
Ptolemy: 40 years. Philadelphus: 38 years. Euergetes: 26 years. Philopator: 17 years. Epiphanes: 24 years.
In his sixteenth year, the fifth millennium was completed. Philometor: 35 years. Euergetes: twenty-nine [years]. Soter: 17
years. Alexander: 10 years. Ptolemy: 8 years. Dionysius: 30 years. Cleopatra: 24 years. End of the account of Ptolemy.
The Roman emperors begin here. Augustus: 40 years. His years in all: 56. Tiberius: 23 years.
Gaius: 4 years. Claudius: 14 years. Nero: 13 years. Vespasian: 10 years. Titus: 2 years.
Domitian: 15 years. Nerva: one. Trajan: 10 years. Hadrian: 21 years. Antoninus: 22
years. Antoninus: 16 years. Commodus: 13 years. Pertinax: 6 months. Severus: 18 years.
Antoninus: seven. Macrinus: one. Antoninus: four. Alexander, son of Mamaea: 13. He was a Christian.
Maximinus: 3 years. Gordian: 6. Philip: 7 years. He too was a Christian. Decius: one. Gallus: two.
Valerian: 15 years. Claudius: one. Aurelian: six. Tacitus: six months. Probus: six. Carus: two.
Diocletian: twenty. Constantine: thirty-three. Constantius, his son: 24. Julian: 2. Jovian: one.
Valens: 14 years. Gratian: one. Theodosius the Great: 16 years. Arcadius: 29. Theodosius the Younger: 26
years. Marcian: seven. Leo: 16 years. Zeno: nineteen. Anastasius: twenty-seven. And in year 16 of their years [?].
Zeno: nineteen. Anastasius: twenty-seven. In the sixteenth year of Anastasius, the sixth millennium was completed. Justin: eight.
Justinian: forty. Justin: eleven. Tiberius: eight. Maurice: 22. Phocas: eight. Heraclius: 31.
Constantine: one. Constantine: 24 years. Constantine: 16. Justinian: ten. Leontius: three.
Tiberius: seven. Justinian: six. Philippicus: 2. Anastasius: 2. Theodosius: one. Leo: twenty-five.
Constantine, his son: thirty-five years. Leo, his son. From Adam to the Flood: two thousand [two hundred and forty-two] years.
From the Flood to Abraham: nine hundred and forty-two years. [The first to reign over] all Asia except India:
Ninus, son of Belus, for fifty-two years. In the forty-third year, Abraham was born. This is Abraham’s first year.
And in Abraham’s sixth year [?], Hanus built Nineveh in the land of Assyria, on the Tigris. He named it Nineveh after himself. Abraham’s seventh year:
There was a war between Ninus, king of Nineveh, and Zoroaster the Magus, king of the Cretans. In Abraham’s tenth year, Ninus, king of Nineveh, died.
His wife Semiramis reigned in his place for forty-two years. Many stories are told about her. She conquered Asia
and constructed mounds because of flooding. Year twenty-two: Semiramis built Babylon. Year forty-five:
The beginning of the forty-first jubilee, according to the reckoning of the Hebrews. Among them, fifty years are called a jubilee.
Thus, according to their account, two thousand years would have elapsed from Adam to this year.
This is what I said: they do not agree with one another’s reckoning, since one reduces the number and another increases it. In Abraham’s fifty-second year:
Semiramis, queen of Nineveh, died. Her son Ninus succeeded her and reigned for thirty-eight years.
In Abraham’s seventy-fifth year, he was granted a revelation of God and the promise made to him.
This was also the first year of the promise. In it Abraham left his father’s household in Haran
and crossed the Euphrates with Sarah his wife. In the seventy-sixth year, there was a great famine, and Abraham went down to Egypt, he
and Sarah his wife. In the eighty-sixth year, Ishmael, the ancestor of the Arabs, was born to Abraham by Hagar.
In the ninetieth year, Ninus, king of Nineveh, died. Arius succeeded him and reigned for thirty years. In Abraham’s hundredth year:
Isaac was born. In the 101st year of Abraham, chief of the prophets, the Word of God appeared in human form
and foretold the calling of the nations, which it brought to fulfillment at the time of Christ’s [?], through the good news of the teaching addressed to all nations.
In Abraham’s 120th year, Arius, king of Nineveh, died. Aralius succeeded him and reigned for forty years.
In Abraham’s 140th year, which was Isaac’s fortieth year, Isaac married Rebekah.
And in the 160th year, two twin sons were born to Isaac by Rebekah: the first was Esau, who is Edom, from whom the Edomites took their name,
and the second was Jacob, from whom came the Israelites, who are the Jews. At this time Melchizedek, king of Salem, was known,
who was a priest of God Most High. In the 160th year, Aralius, king of Assyria, died.
Xerxes succeeded him and reigned for thirty years. At this time the Egyptians made an image of Io and worshipped her.
They also named the river Io after her. At this time Castor, the writer [?] on chronology, was also known.
In the 175th year, which was the hundredth year of the promise, Abraham departed from this world,
at the age of 175 years. In the 176th year, Antioch was built beside the river Orontes by
Casus and Belus, the sons of Inachus. This was the first founding of the city.
In the 190th year, the king of Assyria died. Armamithres succeeded him and reigned for thirty-eight years.
At this time the Egyptians also set up an image of Apis and worshipped him. They called him the god Serapis.
In the 228th year, the king of Assyria died. Belochus succeeded him and reigned for thirty-five years.
At this time Phoroneus, son of Inachus, and Niobe were known, the first to establish laws and courts.
Plato mentions these times as being very ancient, speaking as follows in the discourse called Timaeus:
And when he considered presenting the accounts about people of old, those who belonged to ancient times in this commonwealth,
he [?] to speak about Phoroneus, who was mentioned first, and about Niobe, and about those who came after the flood.
In the year 231, the Telchines and Caryates waged war against Phoroneus and Pharusius.
In the year 236, the city of Athens and Eleusis were built by Ogygus.
In the year 237, Jacob went down to Mesopotamia and worked for Laban for fourteen years.
In the year 246, Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn, was born. In the year 247,
Jacob fathered Simeon and Levi in a single pregnancy. In the year 248,
Jacob fathered Judah, from whom the Jews took their name. In the year 252, Jacob fathered Joseph.
In Joseph’s first year, Jacob was ninety-two years old, and it was the 178th year of the promise.
In the year 256, Messene was built. In the year 258, the flood in the days of Ogygus occurred.
In the year 262, the king of Assyria died, and Balaeus reigned in his place for fifty-two years.
In the year 268, Joseph was sold by his brothers and went down to Egypt.
In the year 276, Memphis in Egypt was built by Apis, king of the Argives.
In the year 279, Apophis became king over Egypt. He saw the dreams that Joseph interpreted.
He made Joseph rule alongside him. In the year 282, Apophis, who was Pharaoh, saw the dreams.
In that same year, Joseph was given authority over Egypt, and this was the first year of abundance.
In the year 286, Isaac departed from this world at the age of 185.
In the year 289, a great famine began throughout the whole earth, during which Joseph distinguished himself.
In the year 290, Jacob entered Egypt, in the 216th year of the promise. In the year 293,
Apophis, the king of Egypt who had made Joseph ruler, died, and Amosis reigned in his place for twenty-five years.
In the year 299, Sparta was built by Spartus, son of Phoroneus. In the year 305,
Jacob departed from this world at the age of 147,
prophesying about Christ and the calling of the nations through him. In the year 317, the king of Egypt died, and Chebron reigned
for thirteen years alongside Joseph. In the year 331, Chebron died, and Amenophis reigned for twenty-one years.
At this time Prometheus became known, the one who is said in the story to have fashioned [?]. For he was wise.
He was changing them from ignorance to education. For this reason they called him the one who fashioned human beings. In the year three hundred and [?]
and two, the king of Egypt died. Another king, Mephres, reigned alongside Joseph for twelve years.
In the 361st year of Abraham, Joseph departed from this world at the age of 110.
He had reigned for eighty of those years. This was also the year [?] and eighty-six from the promise,
from which the years of the Israelites’ enslavement began. In the year 364, Mephres, Joseph’s friend, died.
Misphragmuthosis, an enemy of the Jews, succeeded him as king over Egypt for twenty-six years.
In the year 390, this king died, and Thutmose reigned for nine years. In the year 396,
Surus, king of Syria, became known. Syria was named after him. In the year 400, the king of Egypt died.
Amenothis succeeded him and reigned for thirty-one years. At this time the Ethiopians migrated from the River Indus and settled near Egypt.
Also at this time, when there were many kings over Egypt, Palmanothes reigned in the region of Heliopolis.
He was an enemy of the Jews. He had a daughter named Merris, whom he gave in marriage to Chenephres, king of Memphis.
This is the Raousa who adopted Moses as her son. After Moses grew to manhood, he built Hermopolis and fought the Ethiopians for ten years.
For after the death of Merris, who had adopted Moses, her husband Chenephres plotted against Moses and wanted to kill him.
Merris was buried in Egypt, and the city of Meroë was named after her. When Moses became aware of Chenephres’ plot, he killed Chanethothes,
who had been threatening to kill him. He himself fled to Arabia, to Reuel, and married his daughter, as Artapanus wrote.
In the year 424, Amram fathered Moses when he was seventy years old.
This was the [?] year of the Israelites’ enslavement. In the year 425, the city of Epidaurus was built.
In the year 430, the king of Egypt died. Orus succeeded him and reigned for thirty-eight years.
In the year 450, Xanthus built the city of Trypho-Lesbos [?]. At this time the first Heracles and Cecrops became known.
In the year 466, Moses left Egypt and moved to Reuel. In the year 468,
the king of Egypt died. Achencheres, the daughter of Orus, reigned for twelve years. In the year 475,
the Chaldeans went up to fight the Phoenicians. In the year 480, the queen of Egypt died.
Her brother Athoris reigned for nine years. In the year four hundred and eighty-[?], the city of Athens was built by Doadus.
In the year 483, the flood in Thessaly occurred in the days of Phaethon. In the year 488,
many disasters occurred in Ethiopia, as Plato writes. In the year 490 [?], the king of Egypt died, and Cenchres reigned for sixteen years.
… This was the one who fought against Moses, together with Jannes and Jabus, the sorcerers. Concerning this, Moses said that he drowned Pharaoh and his army in the Red Sea.
In the year 496, the city of Corinth was built. In the year 501, God appeared to Moses on Mount Sinai.
He was sent to Egypt and contended with Pharaoh for five years, performing two signs each year.
[?] and five hundred and two: the temple of Apollo at Delos was established by Erysichthon. In the year 506:
The people went out of Egypt. Moses, when he was eighty years old, was put in charge of bringing the Israelites out of Egypt.
He was with them in the wilderness for forty years, laying down laws for them. At this time Heracles, who was called Dionysus, became known.
The discovery of the vine was made by him. In the year 510, the Areopagus court was established. In the year 511:
Aaron received the high priesthood. He was the first priest. In the year 514, Crete was built.
Apterus, who built it, reigned over it. In the year 526, the temple at Delos was established by Erysichthon son of Cecrops.
In the year 528, Epaphus, son of Io and Zeus, built Memphis when he ruled over the two Egypts.
In the year 530, Lacedaemon was built by Lacedaemon son of Samia. In the year 540, Dardanus built Dardania.
At this time Aegyptus reigned over Egypt; that land was named Egypt after him.
In the year 545, Aaron the high priest departed from this world and was buried on Mount Hor.
His son Eleazar received his high priesthood. In the year 546, Moses also died and was buried on Mount Hor.
Joshua son of Nun took his place. He died at the age of 120, and for forty of those years he led the people.
Here end the five books of Moses, which recount the events of 3,730 years according to the tradition of the Seventy.
At this time Danaus waged war through his fifty daughters and killed the fifty sons of his brother Aegyptus,
except for Lynceus, who reigned after him. There is no doubt about the large number of children among the barbarians, because of the many concubines they take.
In the year 547, the Israelites crossed the Jordan and began slaughtering the inhabitants of that land.
In the year 553, Joshua divided the land of Palestine among the Israelites by lot.
In the year 572, Joshua son of Nun died at the age of 110.
He was buried at Timnath-serah, on Mount [?]. In the year 573, Israel was conquered by the nations.
They served them for eight years. Then Othniel arose and delivered them. Here ends the book of Joshua son of Nun,
which recounts twenty-seven years: the events of the war and the division of the promised land among the Israelites.
In the year 578, Eleazar the high priest died, and they received his priesthood.
Phinehas his son. In the year 581, Othniel arose and delivered the people.
He governed for forty years, including those eight years when the nations ruled over them. In the year 592, Melos and Paphos were built,
and the cities of Thasos and Calliste. In the year 593, Bithynia was built by Phoenix.
In the year 611, Cadmeia and Side were built in Sicily. In the year 612,
Othniel died, and the nations ruled over them for eighteen years. These years too are included in those of Ehud.
In the year 617, the city of Achaea was built by Achaeus. In the year 630, Ehud son of Gera arose
and delivered the people. He judged for eighty years, including those eighteen years when the nations ruled over them. In the year [?]
and seventy, Perseus went to war against the Persians with a large army. In the year 682, the city of Cyrene was built in Libya.
In the year 690, Dionysus went to war against the Indians. He built the city of Nysa beside the river Indus.
In the year 692, Ehud died, and the nations ruled over the Hebrew people for twenty years.
These years too are included in those of Deborah and Baram. In the year 711, the city of Ilion was built by Ilus.
In the year 720, that temple in Eleusis. In that same year, Deborah and Baram fought against Sisera, the commander of the army of Nabin, king of the Ammonites, on Mount Tabor.
The Lord defeated Sisera before Baram. Baram judged for forty years, including those of Nabin. In the year 731, the city of Miletus
was built. In the year 732, Deborah and Baram died, and the Midianites ruled over the people for seven years.
These years are included in those of Gideon. In the year 739, Oreb, Zeeb, Zebah, and Zalmunna came to wage war against Israel.
All these kings gathered and camped in the valley of Jezreel with all their armies. Gideon son of Joash arose and destroyed them all with the sword.
He judged Israel for forty years, including those seven years of the Midianites. In the year 744,
the city of Tyre was built. In that same year, the city of Cyzicus was also built. In the year 772, Gideon died,
and his son Abimelech became king. In the year 773, this Abimelech killed his seventy brothers.
In the year 775, while Abimelech was fighting against Thebez, a woman threw a fragment of an upper millstone down on him and killed him, and he died.
After him, Tola son of Puah arose. He judged Israel for twenty-two years. In the year 797, Tola died.
Jair judged Israel for twenty-two years. In the year 802, the city of Carthage was built by Azorus and Carchedon.
At this time, Minos was laying down laws. In the year 818, Jair died, and Jephthah judged for seven years.
In that same year, Jephthah fought against the Ammonites and the Moabites. He struck them down from Aroer [?] as far as the entrance to Machir, twenty towns,
and as far as Abel-keramim, inflicting a very great defeat. The Ammonites were defeated before the Israelites. In the year 820
And five. Jephthah died, and after him Heshbon, who is Ibzan, judged for seven years. He had thirty sons and thirty [?].
He sent thirty sons outside and brought in thirty brides from outside. In the year 832, Ibzan died.
He was buried in Bethlehem. After him, Elon of Zebulun judged Israel for eight years.
In his days, Ilium was conquered by Alexander. In the year 840, Elon died.
He was buried in Elon. After him, Ekron judged Israel for ten years. Eusebius does not include him in his reckoning.
Although the Book of Judges counts him, he leaves him out. This man had forty sons and thirty daughters.
After this man, the Philistines ruled over the Israelites for forty years, which overlap with the years of the judges.
Afterward Samson arose and judged Israel for forty years. Boaz and Ruth are known at this time.
In the year 845, the city of Alba was built by Ascanius son of Aeneas.
In the year 860, Samson died. After him, Eli the priest judged Israel
for forty years. In the year 873, the Amazons burned the temple at Ephesus.
At this time the Israelites devastated the Benjaminites. In the year 909, Samuel began to prophesy.
In the year 900, Eli the priest died. In that same year, the Philistines devastated the Israelites and also carried away the ark of God with them.
After Eli the priest, Samuel and Saul judged for forty years. At this time Homer the sage is known.
In the year 930, Saul devastated the Amalekites. In the year 933, there was an anointing of
David. In the year 937, Samuel died. In the year 940, there was a war between the Philistines and the Israelites.
The Israelites were defeated by the Philistines. Saul and his sons were also killed in this battle, which took place in the mountains of Gilboa.
After him, David son of Jesse, from the tribe of Judah, reigned as the first king over the Israelites for forty years.
At this time Abiathar the high priest is known, and Gad, Nathan, and Asaph were prophesying.
In the year 962, the city of Magnesia in Asia was built. In the year 965,
the city of Cumae in Italy was built. In the year 967, the city of Myrina was built.
In the year 968, the city of Ephesus was built by Androconus. In the year 971,
the city of Carthage was built by Dido, daughter of Carchedus. In the year 980, King David died.
His son Solomon reigned after him for forty years. In the year 981, the city of Samos was built.
[Up to this point:] the book of Joshua son of Nun, of Judges, and of Samuel, [which recount the] events of 470 years.
From Adam to the flood: 2,242 years.
From the flood to Moses: 1,447 years. And from Moses to the building of the temple:
480 years, according to the reckoning of the Jews. The total of all the years is 4,170.
In the year 984, Solomon began to build the temple in Jerusalem. In the year 990,
the building of the temple was completed. At this time Zadom the priest was known. Zadom and Ahijah the Shilonite were prophesying. In the year 1,000 and [?],
Solomon died, and Rehoboam reigned after him for seventeen years. From this point the Israelites were divided between two kings.
Rehoboam reigned over the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin. From this point all the Israelites also acquired the name Jews.
Jeroboam reigned over the ten tribes. He set up a calf, sinned, and led Israel into sin.
At this time Ahijah and Shemaiah were prophesying in Judah. In the year 1,030, the city of Samosam was built,
and Smyrna was settled. In the year 1,034, the one who lived in Bethel was prophesying,
as was the one at the altar. In the year 1,037, Rehoboam died, and his son Abijah reigned after him for three years.
In the year 1,040, Abijah died, and his son Asa reigned after him for forty-one years. In the year 1,027,
Shishak, king of Egypt, came up against Jerusalem and took all the treasure of the house of the Lord and all the treasure of the kingdom of David and Solomon,
and brought it down to Egypt. In the year 1,047, Zerah the Cushite came up, having also hired the Libyans to accompany him.
They encamped against Judah. King Asa went out against them, pursued them, and slaughtered them with the sword in the valley of Ger.
Those of them who escaped the sword drowned in the sea. At this time Joel son of Iddo was prophesying.
In the year 1,063, there was war between Asa, king of Judah, and Baasha, king of Israel.
He also hired Ben-hadad, king of Syria, to join him. At this time Jehu and Hanani were prophesying. In the year 1,081, there died
Asa, and his son Jehoshaphat reigned after him for twenty-five years. At this time Elijah, Obadiah, Jehu, Micaiah, and Uzziel were prophesying.
False prophets: Zedekiah, Eliezer, and the rest of the four hundred others. In the year 1,090, that drought of Elijah occurred,
lasting three years and six months. There was a great famine throughout the land. In the year 1,106, Jehoshaphat died.
His son Jehoram reigned after him for eight years. At this time Azriel, Eliezer, Elijah, and Elisha were prophesying.
In the year 1,113, Elijah was taken up [?], as if into heaven. In the year 1,115, Jehoram died.
His son Ahaziah reigned after him for one year. In the year 1,116, Jehu killed Ahaziah.
His mother Athaliah reigned after him in Judah for seven years. She openly [?], and men committed adultery with one another's wives.
When there was no [?] of Jezebel and the paganism of the house of Ahab, she did [?] in Jerusalem to the males of the house of David.
At this time Jonadab the priest was known. In the year 1122, the Israelites were considering
whom they should make king over themselves. Jehoiada the priest heard and gathered them into the house of the Lord,
the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds. Jehoiada the priest said to them, “Who ought to be king and sit on David’s throne,
except a king’s son from among David’s descendants?” When he showed them Joash, they rejoiced
with great joy. They brought him down to the house of the Lord and seated him on the royal throne. Athaliah was killed.
He was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned for forty years. Jehu killed Joram and the seventy sons of Ahab and Jezebel.
In the year 1130, Jehoiada the priest died at the age of 130. His son Zechariah succeeded him in the priesthood.
Elisha and this Zechariah the priest were prophesying at this time. In the year 1144,
Hazael, king of Syria, devastated Israel. Again, in the year 1100 and [?], this Hazael gathered an army and oppressed them
throughout the reign of Jehoahaz, king of Israel. In the year 1155, Joash killed Zechariah son of Jehoiada.
In the year 1158, Elisha the prophet died. In the year 1158, Elisha the prophet died.
In the year 1159, the Syrian army plundered Judah and killed their leaders. In the year 1160
and two, Joash was killed by his servants. His son Amaziah succeeded him as king for twenty-nine years. In the year 1163,
Amaziah devastated the Edomites, took their gods, and worshiped them. In the year 1165,
Hazael, king of Syria, died. In the year 1171, the Israelites killed three hundred men of Judah.
In the year 1180, Jonah was sent to Nineveh, and the Ninevites repented.
At this same time Thonos Concolerus, who is called Sardanapalus in Greek, was known as king of Nineveh. Prophesying at this time were
Hosea, Amos—who is Amoz, Isaiah’s father—Jonah, and Nahum. In the year 1185, there was a battle at Tarsus and [?]
between Sardanapalus, king of Nineveh, and Arbaces, king of Media. Sardanapalus was defeated, his army was destroyed, and he himself was killed.
In the year 1190, Amaziah was killed by the Jews with a spear. His son Uzziah succeeded him as king for fifty-two years.
In the year 1205, Uzziah, king of Judah, demolished in battle the walls of Gath, Azotus, and Jamnia.
He also fought against the Arabs who lived in Petra. Jonah, Hosea, Amos, and Isaiah were prophesying at this time.
Hesiod was also known, as Porphyry wrote. In the year 1211 from Abraham,
King Uzziah entered God’s temple to offer incense. When he was [?] by Azariah the priest and refused to leave, he suddenly became leprous all over.
And [?] was stopped from prophesying. In the year 1,224, Pul, king of the Assyrians,
marched against Samaria. After receiving a thousand talents of silver from Menahem, king of Israel, he withdrew.
In the year 1,240 from Abraham, the first Olympiad began. In the year 1,241,
Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, marched against the land of Judah and deported many of the Hebrews to Assyria.
In the year 1,243, Uzziah died, and his son Jotham succeeded him as king for sixteen years.
In the year 1,246, the cities of Pandosia and Metapontium were founded in Italy.
In the year 1,249, the first ship for Cyprus [?] was built at Athens. Those prophesying at this time were Hosea
and Isaiah, Joel, Oded, and Micah. In the year 1,259, Jotham died,
and his son Ahaz succeeded him as king for sixteen years. In the year 1,260, the cities of Selinus and Zancle were founded in Sicily.
In that same year, war broke out between Pekah and Ahaz, and Pekah killed 120,000 Jews. In the year 1,262,
Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, king of Israel, fought against Ahaz and took many Jews captive.
In the year 1,263, the people of Judah were taken captive by the Edomites. In the year 1,265,
Ahaz sent word to Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, asking him to come to his aid. When he came, he killed Rezin, and they took the Syrians captive.
He also took a large amount of silver from Ahaz and withdrew. In the year 1,267, Rome was founded by Romulus,
after whom the entire Latin people were also named Romans. In the year 1,269 [?],
Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, marched against Samaria and took the ten tribes of Israel captive.
He deported them to the land of the Medes and the Chaldeans. He sent Assyrians into the towns to guard the land of the Jews.
Because they were being killed by lions, the king of Assyria sent them Aur the priest to teach them the laws. These are the Samaritans,
for the name “Samaritans” itself means “keepers and guardians.” In the year 1,275, Ahaz died,
and his son Hezekiah succeeded him as king for twenty-nine years. In that same year, the city of Naxos was founded in Sicily.
In the year 1,277, Hezekiah celebrated the Passover. In the year 1,282,
Sennacherib, king of Assyria, marched against Jerusalem and the cities of Judah and besieged them.
But the angel of God destroyed 185,000 men from his army. When he heard that Tirhakah [?], king of the Cushites, had also set out to fight against him,
he withdrew to Nineveh, and his sons killed him there. In that same year, the cities of Syracuse and Catania were founded in Sicily.
In that same year, the Lacedaemonians conquered [?]. In the year 1,285.
The cities of Leontini, Megara, and Martonia in Sicily were founded. In the year 1289, Hezekiah became ill. And because he asked for a sign,
the sun went backward fifteen degrees. In the year 1293, Merodach-baladan, king of Babylon, sent gifts to Hezekiah.
In the year 1300, the city of Cronosus was founded in Sicily. In the year 1304, Hezekiah died.
His son Manasseh reigned after him for fifty-five years. The city of Nicomedia was founded, and the Sibyl became known. In the year 1307,
the cities of Croton, Parium, Sybaris [?], and Ecbatana were founded. In the year 1310 of Abraham,
Numa Pompilius built the Capitol from its foundations. The Parthenians [?] built Tarentum, and the Corinthians built Corcyra.
In the year 1306, the commanders of the Assyrian army took Manasseh, king of Judah, captive and brought him down to Babylon.
In that same year, Gela was founded in Sicily, and Phaselis in Pamphylia. In the year 1330, the city of Chalcedon was founded.
In the year 1342, while Manasseh was in captivity, he turned to the God of his ancestors. He went up and was restored to
his position and his kingdom. In that same year, the city of Cyzicus was founded, and the city of Locri in Italy.
In the year 1359, Manasseh died. His son Amon reigned after him for twelve years according to the translation of the Seventy,
and for two years according to the Hebrews. Manasseh, king of Judah, became enraged at Isaiah and sent wicked men,
and they sawed him with a saw inside a tree, from his head to his feet. He was 120 years old when they sawed him.
He had been a prophet of God for ninety years. In the year 1360, the city of Istros was founded in Pontus. In the year 1363,
the cities of Acanthus, Stagira, Lampsacus, and Abdera were founded. In the year 1367,
the city of Selinus was founded in Sicily. In the year 1370, the city of Borysthenes was founded in Pontus.
In the year 1371, Amon died. His son Josiah reigned after him for thirty-one years. Hilkiah the high priest was becoming known.
Zephaniah was prophesying. In the year 1384, Jeremiah began to prophesy. In that same year, Battus founded Cyrene.
In the year 1386, the city of Sinope was founded. In the year 1388, the city of Lipara was founded. In the year 1389,
Josiah celebrated the Passover. In that same year, the city of Dyrrhachium was founded. Jeremiah, Zephaniah, and Huldah were prophesying at this time.
In the year 1401, Pharaoh Neco went up and fought a battle with Josiah by the Euphrates. Josiah was also killed by him.
His son Jehoahaz reigned after him for three months. Pharaoh took him to Egypt, and his brother Jehoiakim reigned after him for twelve years.
In the year 1405, Nebuchadnezzar went up and conquered Jerusalem, and brought down a great number of
captives. He also brought down with him the vessels used for worship. He imposed tribute on Jehoiakim and departed.
In this same captivity, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, the sons of Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, went down.
And Daniel, the son of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, to Babylon. In the year 1412, Nebuchadnezzar again went up and captured Judah.
They led many of the Jews into captivity and plundered many of the sacred vessels. He imposed tribute on Jehoiakim and removed him.
In the year 1414, Jehoiakim died, and his son Jeconiah became king. In the third month of his reign,
Nebuchadnezzar again went up against him, took him and many of the people captive, and brought him down to Babylon. At this time, at this time, those prophesying were:
Uriah, whom Jehoiakim killed, and Jeremiah in Judah; and in Babylon, Daniel, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael.
Zedekiah reigned for eleven years in place of Jeconiah, his brother’s son. In the year 1416 of Abraham.
The city of Camarina was built. The city of Perinthus was also built. Those prophesying in Babylon were:
Daniel and his companions; and in Judah, Jeremiah and Baruch. In the year 1419, Ezekiel began to prophesy.
The city of Massalia was built. The false prophet: Hananiah. Solon the lawgiver became known. In the year 1426,
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, went up and took captive the whole western land, from the Euphrates to the sea. He entered the islands of the sea,
took captives, demolished Tyre, and burned it with fire. He killed Hiram, king of Tyre. He entered Egypt in pursuit of the Israelites,
who had taken refuge with Pharaoh, king of Egypt. He devastated Egypt and took the Israelites captive. When he came out from the sea,
he conquered Jerusalem, and God delivered Zedekiah into his hands. He killed his sons before him, while he watched them, at Riblah
in Hamath. He blinded Zedekiah himself and sent him to Babylon. Nebuzaradan, the chief executioner, demolished the wall of Jerusalem
and burned the temple of the Lord with fire. He took the bronze, iron, and vessels with him to Babylon.
Simeon the high priest, because he had freedom to speak with the chief executioner, persuaded him, and he gave him all the books of the Scriptures and did not burn them with fire.
Simeon the high priest gathered them and put them in a well. He filled a tall bronze brazier with fire and placed it in the well. And Jerusalem was devastated.
This is Simeon the high priest, who was bound by the Holy Spirit not to see death until he had seen the Messiah, as some people say.
The birth of the Messiah, however, was 591 years away from this time. There is no reason to doubt this.
For Hiram, king of Tyre, of whom they say that he was the one whom Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, killed in this year,
was the friend of David and of his son Solomon. Now, from the time of David until this year there were 486 years.
And if this man lived so long, why is there doubt about the one who was bound by the Holy Spirit? In the year 1440 of Abraham.
Daniel and Ezekiel were prophesying in Babylon, and Jeremiah and Baruch in Judah. The false prophets: Ahab, Zedekiah, and Shimei.
In the year 1449, Nebuchadnezzar died, and Evil-merodach became king. Jeremiah was prophesying in Egypt. Aesop, the writer of fables, became known.
In the year 1452, Evil-merodach brought Jeconiah out of prison and established him in honor. He married Giuth, the daughter of Eliakim.
And he fathered Shealtiel by her. Concerning this, Scripture says, “Josiah fathered Jeconiah and his brothers during the exile in Babylon.” And Shealtiel took for himself
a wife, Hatibath, the daughter of Elkanah, and fathered by her Zerubbabel, who came up with the people from Babylon. In the year 1,454,
Evil-merodach died, and Belshazzar became king after him. In the year 1,456, Daniel interpreted the writing for him, and that very night he was killed.
Cyrus the Persian took over his kingdom for thirty years. Cyrus the Persian brought the captives up from Babylon, as many as fifty thousand, and set up the altar.
And he laid the foundations of the temple. But because the nations around them hindered them, the work remained unfinished until King Darius.
The entire period of the Jewish people's captivity amounted to seventy years. According to some people's reckoning, these extended from the third year of Jehoiakim
until the nineteenth year of Cyrus. According to the reckoning of others, however, they began at the beginning of Jeremiah's prophetic ministry,
which began in the thirteenth year of Josiah. From the fifth year of Jeremiah's prophetic ministry until the first year of Cyrus,
there were seventy years. But the seventy years of the temple's desolation were completed in the days of Darius, counting from the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
At this time Daniel and Ezekiel were prophesying in Babylon, and Habakkuk, Haggai, and Zechariah in Judah. Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest,
and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, the leader of the people, were well known. At this time Susanna gained distinction. Pherecydes, the teacher of Pythagoras. A city
was built by the people of Samos. In the year 1,485, Tomyris, a woman who was queen, killed Cyrus. Cambyses became king for eight years.
Among the Hebrews, Cambyses is said to be called Nebuchadnezzar the Second. They say that the events of the story of Judith took place in his days.
In the year 1,493, Holofernes, Nebuchadnezzar's army commander, marched against all Syria
and took captives, killed people, and devastated it. He was killed by Judith the Hebrew woman. Anyone who wishes to read and learn about the atrocities he committed
should read the story of Judith. In this same year Cambyses died, and the Magian brothers held the kingdom for seven months.
After them Darius held it for thirty-six years. Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi were prophesying among the Hebrews.
In the year 1,495, the people who had remained behind since Cyrus came up from Babylon. In the year 1,500,
the construction of the temple was completed through the prophecy of Haggai and Zechariah. In the year 1,521, Pythagoras the philosopher died,
having lived ninety-five years. In the year 1,529, Darius died, and his son Xerxes became king after him for twenty years.
In the year 1,537, the battle at Thermopylae took place, as did the engagement off Salamis.

He was the one about whom Mar Isaac also composed many discourses. Year 1569.

In the year 1550, a stone fell in the rivers of Aegos. Year 1583.
The work of rebuilding the city and the wall was completed by Nehemiah the cupbearer. Socrates and Democritus became known. Year 1587.

In the year 1591, when severe earthquakes occurred, Atalanta [?], near Locris, was shaken and became an island.

Darius died, and his son Artaxerxes reigned for forty years. It seems to me that the story of Esther belongs to his days.

Alexander of Pherae also lived at this time. In the year one thousand and [?] hundred and sixty-two from Abraham.
Alexander, son of Philip the Macedonian, was born. In the year 1650, Artaxerxes died.
Ochus reigned for twenty-seven years. In the year 1673, there died
Plato. In the year 1676, Ochus died, and Arses reigned for four years. Year 1665.
Egypt was conquered by Ochus, king of the Persians. In the year 1669, Ochus destroyed Sidon.
Jaddua, the high priest of the Jews, became known. In the year 1680, Manasseh, the brother of Jaddua the high priest, built a temple on Mount Gerizim.
In this same year Arses died, and Darius reigned over the Persians for six years. And in this very same year,
Philip, king of the Macedonians, also died. After him his son Alexander reigned over Macedonia for twelve years and six months.
In the year 1681, Alexander set out to travel through the earth and conquer nations and kingdoms. From the history of Alexander.
When he wished to set out and travel through the earth, he stood up, made a vow, and said, “If the Messiah, the Son of God, comes in my days, I will worship him,
I and all my armies, and we will serve him. And if he does not come in my days, this crown on my head and this throne of my kingdom
shall be his, for his honor, when he comes. And these eighty pounds of gold shall be his for incense, lamps, and offerings when he comes.”
He rose, took with him an army of three hundred and twenty-four thousand, and went to Egypt; and craftsmen [?]. He crossed over and traveled for twelve days.
And he found a plain whose circuit was [?] twelve miles, and that Dead Sea. He could not go any farther, because they saw that those who approached
the Dead Sea died. He went up and traveled through that plain, as it is written in the account, as far as the place where the sun sets.
They saw the sun high in the sky, and things like balls of fire were falling from it at that [?]. And all the inhabitants of that country,
along with the animals and birds, fled into caves. Then Alexander and his entire army set out again, and he turned to go east.
He passed through many countries, until he reached a country situated between the kingdoms of the Romans and the Persians
and the territory of Gog. Alexander sent messengers to say, “The king of the Greeks is passing through. He takes no captives and causes no destruction.
Let everyone remain in peace. Only the very old men who are in the country should come to me, because I want to ask them something.”
When they came, he said to them, “Whose country is this?” They said to him, “It belongs to Darius, king of Persia.” He said to them, “And this great, mighty mountain—
what do you call it?” They said to him, “This is the boundary that God established between us and those nations on its other side.
It extends like this as far as inner India. These nations that are here, on its other side, are sorcerers. When they want to go out to war,
they place a pregnant woman in front of a fire until her child comes out. They perform sorcery over it and dip their weapons.
Then one of them appears like two hundred horsemen, and their voices are like jackals.” Alexander said to them,
“Have they come out in your lifetime?” They said to him, “There is a breach in this mountain about ten cubits wide, and they come out through it from time to time.
These Persian fortresses that you see—they destroyed them.” He said to them, “And what are the names of their kings?” They said to him,
“Gog, Magog, Gig, Tamrat, and Tamratan. Beyond them are the people of Amazrat, and beyond them are the people of Kalb-Barnash, and beyond them are the people of Mahnai.
Beyond them there are no human beings, but only a desolate wilderness, great mountains, dragons, and wild animals. Beyond them is the paradise of God,
far away in an elevated place. It appears to be situated between earth and heaven. By night and by day, light can be seen from there at a distance.”
He said to them, “And these rivers—the Euphrates, the Tigris, the Pishon, and the Gihon—how does Scripture say that they flow out from there?”
They said to him, “The Lord brought the rivers out of paradise. And so that human beings would not travel along them and enter paradise,
God commanded these rivers to descend and travel underground for many [?],
and then to go on, emerge, and become visible outside in places far apart from one another.” When Alexander had heard many things from them, he let them go.
He gave orders to all the craftsmen whom he had brought from Egypt, and he made a great iron gate in that very breach in the mountain.
They covered it with iron and secured it with clamps. But those old men who had left him went to Darius and told him.
He sent and assembled eighty-two kings and their armies, and they came against him. While he was sleeping until noon and resting,
he and all his armies, the Son of God approached him and woke him. He said to him, “Why are you sleeping?” And he was very frightened.
And he said to him, “What do you want, my lord?” He said to him, “I am the Lord to whom you made a vow, and in whose name you set out.”
“And now kings and their armies are coming against you. But when they come, call on me, and I will come to your aid.” Then he arose and awakened
his nobles and said to them, “Just now the Lord appeared to me and said to me, ‘Look, kings and their armies are coming against you.'
“‘But call on me, and I will come to your aid, for I am the Lord to whom you made a vow, and in whose name you set out.’
“But let us go up to the top of this mountain and see.” Some of their men went up and saw that the whole land was covered with armies.
They hurried down and said, “What are we to do? The whole land is covered with armies coming against us!”
Then Alexander arose and commanded all his troops to offer incense to the Lord who had appeared to him and to call on him.
For Alexander said, “Let the Lord come and find the camp [?] sweet-smelling.”
Alexander placed his crown, his robe, and his royal power on the ground and said, “God, yours is the kingdom, and yours is the earth.” And he said,
“God, yours is the kingdom, and yours is the victory. Come to our aid!” While they were standing there, the armies surrounded them on every side.
Then Alexander and his troops cried out, “The battle and the victory belong to the Lord!” Again they cried out and said, “Lord, come to our aid!”
And Alexander said, “Lord, who appeared to me and said to me, ‘Call on me, and I will come to your aid,'
“come to our aid at this very hour!” Then they saw him coming on a chariot of cherubim, with a multitude of angels on his right and on his left.
There was a great battle. The Lord approached Alexander and said to him, “Do not be afraid. Look, I am with you.”
The Lord’s voice rang out, raging amid the troops among the mountains. Alexander’s men killed sixty-two kings and their armies from among them.
They captured alive the king of Persia who had gathered them together. Alexander wanted to kill him. He said to him,
“What will you gain by killing me? Take for yourself the gold, the silver, and everything in my kingdom. I will make Persia subject to you
“for fifteen years.” Then he arose, went down, and conquered the land of Persia as well. He went down to India. Afterward Alexander, Darius, and Shapur agreed among themselves
that each of them would station six thousand guards at the gate that Alexander had built to keep out the people of Gog.
After fifteen years, Assyria would be its own mistress. He returned to his land in great triumph.
He went and prayed in Jerusalem and fulfilled his vows, giving thanks to the Lord in whose name he had set out and who had given him all this victory.
He departed from there and went to Alexandria, where he took his seat on his royal throne. The year one thousand six hundred and eighty-one.
Alexander conquered the Illyrians and the Thracians. He demolished Thebes and destroyed its people. He prevailed over the Persians and captured Sardis.
He defeated the king’s generals at the Granicus River. The year one thousand six hundred and eighty-three. Alexander conquered Tyre
and demolished the cities of the Jews. When he was received by the Jews and offered sacrifice to God, he honored Andromachus the priest and put him in charge of the places.
When the inhabitants of Marin had killed this man, [Alexander came from] Egypt and captured the city. He settled Macedonians in it.
[Year 1,000 and [?].] Darius and Alexander fought a great battle. [?] Sopholus [?] Darius was defeated. [?] In this same year:
Alexander built Alexandria in the land of Egypt. At this time Anaximenes, Epicurus, and Aristotle were known.
Year 1889. Alexander conquered the Hyrcanians and the Mardi. When he went up to Ammonaus, he built Paraetonium.
Year 1690. Alexander captured the rock of Aornos and crossed the river Indus. Year 1691.
Alexander and Pul, king of the Indians, fought a battle. Pul was killed, and all India was conquered. Year 1692 of Abraham.
Alexander died in Babylon at the age of thirty-two. After him the kingdom was divided among many rulers. The era of the Ptolemies.
The era of Alexander was also reckoned from this point, from the first year in which his brother Philip became king over the Macedonians.

Antigonus became king over Asia and Syria. Year 1696.
Ptolemy, king of Egypt, advanced through cunning and deception and captured Jerusalem, the city of the Jews.
He took many of them captive and settled them in Egypt. Onias the high priest was known. Year 1700.
Antioch was built beside the river Orontes by Antigonus, king of Syria. Year 1701.
Seleucus Nicator was the first to reign over Syria, Babylon, and the upper regions, for thirty-two years. Year 1705.
The Hebrew book of Maccabees counts the years of the Greek kingdom from this year, among the years recorded for them in the divine book.
The people of Edessa reckon the era from the year 1706. Year 1708. The city of Lysimachia in Thrace was built.
In the same year Cyprus was conquered by Ptolemy. Theodorus, the Atheist, was
known. Year 1712. Seleucus built these cities: Antioch, Laodicea, and Seleucia,
and Apamea, Edessa, and Aleppo. He built a little of Amida, and [?]. Year 1716. Seleucus conquered Babylon.
